Hi Marissa / Alex —

Thanks for the ping. Quick summary and attachments — please see the attached sanitized executive pen test summary and our vulnerability management process document. High-level bullets below: 

Pen test (most recent):
- Vendor: GoodSec (third-party)
- Date: June 2026 (external, black-box + authenticated components)
- Scope: public endpoints, tenant-isolated control plane, representative API surface
- Findings (sanitized): 0 critical, 0 high, 3 medium (information exposure / auth checks), 7 low.
- Remediation: All medium findings were addressed within our standard SLA windows; no open criticals.
- Full technical report: available under NDA and with redaction on customer identifiers.

Vulnerability management process (see vuln_mgmt_process.pdf):
- Scanning cadence: weekly unauthenticated external scans, monthly authenticated scans for staging and production, SCA (software composition analysis) on every PR + weekly dependency scans, container image scans on build.
- SLAs (time-to-fix by severity): Critical: 72 hours (hotfix), High: 14 days, Medium: 30 days, Low: triaged per release cycle.
- Verification: Fixes are verified by automated regression tests + follow-up scan; we require closure evidence (ticket + patch details) before sign-off.
- Disclosure policy: Coordinated disclosure with researchers; standard 90-day vulnerability disclosure timeline unless critical exploitation observed. We engage customers directly for incidents affecting them.

Attachments included (sanitized): pen_test_report_redwood_june2026_summary.pdf, vuln_mgmt_process.pdf

If you need the original pen test or additional logs we can provide under NDA. Happy to join the 11/30 call to walk through details — I’m available 11/30 10–11 PT.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
